MECHANISM UPDATE — every single-factor theory is now falsified; the fix stays scoped by observation. Controlled test (local, throwaway fresh label, /bin/sleep 30 as Program, LimitLoadToSessionType=Aqua): `launchctl bootstrap gui/501` → exit 0, loaded. So bootstrap does NOT categorically refuse key-carrying plists. Falsified to date: (1) categorical key refusal (sleep test + host.v1 both load with Aqua); (2) .app-Program discriminator (home's failing helper is a plain Caskroom CLI binary); (3) per-label launchd wedge (home's label was virgin). Updated matrix rows: [.app + Aqua + Aqua session → EIO], [plain + Background + SSH context → EIO], [plain + Aqua + Aqua session → loads ×3 incl. fresh non-fleet label], [no key → loads]. Two failure cells, plausibly two distinct launchd behaviors; untested cells include Aqua-key bootstrap from an SSH context — which is exactly what the yasyf box's captain-hook upgrade over SSH would exercise against host.v1.

The ratified fix (Background→ProcessType, Aqua→dropped, uniformly) survives falsification because it eliminates the key from every emitted agent, covering both observed failure cells and the untested SSH/Aqua cell; key REMOVAL is proven safe in every tested configuration. host.v1 drops its key deliberately despite being a healthy carrier — redundant in the gui domain, and carrying it through an SSH-context upgrade is the untested risk cell.

Also: the wasmtime hook error is filed (captain-hook fdebd37 — CWD-shadowing sys.path bug, spawnllm working tree shadows the venv copy), and the post-bootstrap `bridge failed: disconnected` has its own new daemonkit backlog bug (Swift BrokerSocketBridge EAGAIN-as-fatal) — distinct from this task.
